fixes.explanation: His brothers and the rest of his father's household hear about it, and they go down to him there. The text doesn't say why they came, so I won't tell you. I think it had to mean something that family showed up at a cave. Nobody mails a card to a cave, so showing up in person says a lot.
Nothing in the text says they report David to anybody. The verse says they heard about it and went down to him there. David's family walks toward him, not toward Saul.
That's the opposite of what happens. The text says they went down to David at the cave. They didn't keep away. They made the trip.

Leader is right. Everyone who was distressed or indebted or discontented rallied around David, and he became their leader. About four hundred men were with him. David went to a cave for refuge and ended up with a crowd, which is the least quiet refuge I've ever heard of.
The text doesn't call David their servant. It says he became their leader. About four hundred men rallied around him, and nobody was handing him a towel. They gathered to him.

Gad, a prophet, tells David, “Do not stay in the stronghold. Depart and go into the land of Judah.” David leaves and goes to the forest of Hereth. Gad says go, and the very next thing the text says is that David left.
Gad says the opposite. His words are, “Do not stay in the stronghold.” The word for David is to go, and the place he's told to go is the land of Judah. David leaves and goes to the forest of Hereth.

Gad never sends David back to Gath. He says to go into the land of Judah. Going back to Achish, the king of Gath, would also mean returning to the place where David acted insane in front of him (1 Samuel 21:10-15). That would be a hard thing to explain at the door.

Doeg the Edomite says, “I saw the son of Jesse come to Ahimelech son of Ahitub at Nob.” Ahimelech is the priest at Nob. Doeg is with Saul's servants when he says what he saw. I think it got very quiet right after that.

Doeg says nothing about Jonathan, Saul's son (1 Samuel 14:1), or any field. His report is that he saw the son of Jesse come to Ahimelech son of Ahitub at Nob. Saul had already complained about his son's covenant with David, but that's not the part Doeg speaks up about.

Peace isn't what Saul says. He says it was “…so that he could rise up against me to lie in wait, as he is doing today.” That's Saul's accusation that David is lying in wait against him. Peace isn't anywhere in his charge.

Ahimelech says it right to Saul's face: “Who among all your servants is as faithful as David, the king’s son-in-law, the captain of your bodyguard and honored in your house?” Saul is the king, and this is a priest talking to him. That's some nerve, talking like that to the king. Ahimelech says it anyway.

Ahimelech says, “…your servant knew nothing of this whole affair—not in part or in whole.” He asks the king not to accuse him or anyone in his father's household. He's pleading, and he says he himself knew nothing. It's the plainest way to say it.

False is right, and it's a heavy one. Saul answers Ahimelech, “You will surely die, Ahimelech, you and all your father’s house!” He doesn't spare Ahimelech after hearing the plea. I think this is a hard verse to sit with.
